title: SNAP work-requirement and time-limit gate · first pass

selection_contract.declared_universe: Federal SNAP statutes, implementing rules and memoranda, recipient-rights materials, administrative data, and federal program evaluations that define or test work-based eligibility categories.
selection_contract.selection_reason: The gate explicitly distinguishes adults classified as able to work, converts that classification into benefit eligibility and time limits, contains exceptions and waivers, and provides formal review routes.

sources.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 · SNAP implementation
retrieved_facts: FNS identifies current implementation materials for SNAP work requirements, ABAWD exceptions, waiver criteria, and alien eligibility under the 2025 law.
The implementation index establishes the current rulemaking and guidance surface but not a complete affected-person outcome denominator.

sources.title: SNAP: A Primer on Eligibility and Benefits
retrieved_facts: Current law applies general work requirements to many nondisabled adults through age 64 and expands the three-month time limit to additional adults and households.
The source distinguishes general work requirements from the stricter three-month time limit.
It reports population denominators for nondisabled adult participants and describes statutory exceptions.

sources.title: USDA Reiterates Importance of Those Who Can Work, Should Work While Receiving SNAP
retrieved_facts: The Department publicly framed the policy around work, dependency, self-sufficiency, idleness, and program integrity.
The memorandum addressed the Secretary's waiver authority and state implementation.
The frame does not by itself establish racial hierarchy, unlawful discrimination, or an improper gate.

sources.title: SNAP Work Requirements
retrieved_facts: The program distinguishes general work requirements from the ABAWD work requirement and time limit.
The page identifies work, training, workfare, exemptions, disqualification, loss of benefits, and routes for regaining eligibility.
The public page must be reconciled with later 2025 implementation guidance wherever age and exception criteria changed.

sources.title: SNAP Eligibility and Fair Hearing Rights
retrieved_facts: A recipient may request a fair hearing within 90 days of a disputed local SNAP decision.
A fair hearing can test whether the case decision was correctly made but cannot change governing law or regulation.

sources.title: The Impact of SNAP ABAWD Time Limit Reinstatement in Nine States
retrieved_facts: The study reports substantial reductions in SNAP participation after time-limit reinstatement.
The study reports no evidence that the time limit increased employment or annual earnings.
The evaluation is a bounded multi-state study and does not by itself establish the current nationwide effect of the 2025 law.

sources.title: Understanding How State Agencies Determine SNAP Participants' Fitness for Work
retrieved_facts: The study documents state-level screening and verification practices for physical or mental limitations.
It reports staff discretion and cross-state variation in fitness-for-work determinations.
The study creates a selector-implementation denominator but not a complete current outcome and correction ledger.
